text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* A high-speed Milan-Rome train hurtled off the track and crashed into electricity pylons near the Northern Italy station of Piacenza, killing at least eight people and injurying 30 (all).
* Franco Marini was elected secretary general of the Popular party, a moderate political movement supporting the ruling coalition (all).
* Opposition Freedom Alliance's deputies are due to meet tomorrow and find a common position on the proposal of an all-party bicameral commission to carry out constitutional reforms (all).
* A consortium led by Ea-Generali was defeated in a bid for the sell-off of Austrian bank Creditanstalt as the government preferred a rival offer put forward by Bank Austria (all).

* Engineering employers association Federmeccanica is expected to meet tomorrow to discuss a long-running row over metalworkers' contract renewal. Federmeccanica rejected as too high a government'proposal for a 200,000 lire pay rise (all).

* In an interview, Chicco Testa, chairman of state electricity group Enel, says talks are under way with France Telecom, At&t, Cable & Wireless and Unisource for a possible partnership in telecommunications. "We intend to concentrate on fixed and mobile phones. This is not a commitment linked only to short-term objectives, such as the bid for a third phone operator" (La Stampa).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
